findings.summary: A contact submission rejected by the Invisible Captcha timestamp check redirects with flash[:error], which the contact page never renders, so the failure is invisible.
findings.fix: Set on_timestamp_spam to a ContactsController method that builds ContactMessage from the posted params, sets flash.now[:alert] to "Sorry, that was too quick! Please resubmit.", and renders pages/contact. The template prints flash[:alert] only, never flash[:error].

findings.summary: When the contact email fails the model format check, the associated field error is only "is invalid" and does not show an acceptable address.
findings.fix: Set the email format message to "Enter an email address in the format name@example.com." Keep rendering it in #contact-email-error. The email field already points aria-describedby at that id when the model has errors.

findings.summary: The contact and manage-link honeypot is hidden by a random CSS strategy that often leaves a labeled text field in the accessibility tree, and filling it returns a success notice.
findings.fix: Render both honeypots inside a hidden container, as app/views/gauges/_alert_signup.html.erb does, instead of Invisible Captcha's off-screen or 1px-clip CSS. A filled honeypot currently hits spam_detected and shows a success notice.

findings.summary: A server-side station signup failure only shows "Could not save subscription." The email field is not aria-invalid and has no aria-describedby error.
findings.fix: Re-render the signup form with the submitted email instead of redirecting to signup=invalid. Set aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby="gauge-alert-email-error" on #gauge-alert-email, and put the error text in an element with that id.

findings.summary: The signup error "Could not save subscription." does not tell the user how to correct the email address.
findings.fix: Change ALERTS["invalid"] to "Enter an email address in the format name@example.com." Associate that text with #gauge-alert-email through aria-describedby, and do not rely on the generic sentence alone.

findings.summary: Map station search can leave aria-activedescendant pointing at an option that renderSearchResults has already removed.
findings.fix: Remove aria-activedescendant whenever results are cleared, empty, or replaced, including the early returns in renderSearchResults and closeMobileSearch. The home search controller already does this in clearActiveDescendant.

findings.summary: The home search listbox includes a Browse all stations on map link that is not a listbox option, so the popup role does not match its contents.
findings.fix: Render that footer link as a sibling after #home-search-results, not inside the role=listbox element. Leave only role=option nodes in the listbox.

findings.summary: Closing the map search hides the panel while keyboard focus is inside it and does not move focus back to the Search stations button.
findings.fix: In closeMobileSearch, if the panel contains document.activeElement, move focus to the .map-search-toggle button after hiding the panel. That button is the control that opened the search.

passed: Contact name, email, subject, and message have explicit label for/id pairs. Placeholders are hints, not the only name.
Contact name uses autocomplete=name and email uses autocomplete=email. Signup and manage-link email fields use autocomplete=email.
Contact fields and both public email fields set required. Search fields are optional and omit required.
Contact model errors set aria-invalid=true and aria-describedby to the matching field-error id, and the re-render keeps the posted values.
The signup checkbox Include in daily digest is wrapped in its label. No radio group is in these forms.
Home and map search inputs have aria-label Search stations. Directory search on alerts and state pages has a label for station-search.
Home search supports Arrow Up/Down, Enter, and Escape, keeps focus on the input, and clears aria-activedescendant when the list closes. Map search uses the same arrow keys while the input is focused.
Directory checkbox groups expose a group name with role=group and aria-label, and each checkbox has its own label.
Submit controls are native submit buttons or inputs. No password, file, or date fields are in scope.
The gauge signup honeypot is inside a hidden element, with a label and tabindex=-1.
application.html.erb has no form controls. No multi-step wizard is implemented for these forms.
notes: Nothing moves focus to the first invalid field after contact, signup, or manage-link errors. Those are full-page responses with the error text in the document, so this was not scored as a failure of 3.3.1.

Posted email is discarded on the contact too-fast redirect, on station signup redirects, and when the manage-link bot check re-renders without setting @email. There is no multi-step wizard. This was not scored as 3.3.7, whose intent is multi-step processes; preserve the values while fixing the error text.

Browser constraint validation can block an empty or obviously malformed email before submit. The server messages above are what render when that check is bypassed or the model still rejects the value.
Turnstile's aria-label sits on a generic div, which browsers do not expose. The injected iframe title was not verified. Bot-check text is visible and is not tied to the widget with aria-describedby.
Invisible Captcha picks display:none, off-screen, or a 1px clip at random, so the honeypot is not in the accessibility tree on every render.

Directory filtering writes the match count into a polite live region on every keystroke, including connect. A failed home or map search response leaves the UI unchanged and shows no error. Neither was scored as 4.1.3.
Map search binds Enter twice: submitSearch always opens the first match, and the document keydown handler clicks the highlighted option. Which navigation wins was not executed.
Home and map result rows are links with role=option, so Tab can walk every result as well as the arrow keys. Not scored as a failure.

Searches are not wrapped in a search element. Checkbox groups use role=group and aria-label rather than fieldset and legend. Required fields have no visible required text. The required attribute is set.
subscription_timezone_controller.js only writes a hidden time_zone on the public signup form. Admin login and tokenized manage and unsubscribe pages were not reviewed.
